questions.q: What joins a CRM company to its Intact account?
o: The Account code — the Intact A/C code stored on the company
questions.e: Account code is the join key. Names and domains drift and duplicate; the A/C code does not.

questions.q: Which of these can Customer Operations resolve alone, with no approval?
o: Giving a customer a discount to win the order
Agreeing 30 day credit terms for a new account
Giving stock and lead times from Intact and chasing a courier
Issuing a credit note as a goodwill gesture
questions.e: Stock, lead times, supplier and courier chasing, order confirmations, standard quotes within the rules and standard returns are all resolve-alone. Discounts and credit terms need sales approval; new credit accounts and larger credit notes need management.

questions.q: Who decides the price on a standard quotation?
o: Customer Operations, within the agreed rules
The salesperson — Operations builds and sends the rest
questions.e: Operations prepares the quotation in Intact and sends it from sales@; the salesperson decides the price only. If it is the same price as last time, Operations checks Intact and sends.

questions.q: Can you rely on the Sales Transaction object for a customer's spend history?
o: Yes, it is fed live from Intact
No — it is currently empty, the Intact backfill has not run
No — the object does not exist
questions.e: The object exists and is designed to join to Intact on the same Account code, but it has not been populated. Until the backfill runs, take the numbers from Intact.
